subject: Executive signoff: temporary availability variance & tiered service-credit for Helix Labs
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-09-19T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary availability variance + tiered credit for Helix Labs evaluation

Team —

Helix Labs (Sam Torres, Alicia Ng) asked for a temporary tweak to our SLA for their 6-week evaluation. Key ask from the customer: allow a controlled availability tolerance while they run sustained throughput tests that spike p95 latency and produce transient KV cache thrash. In return they're asking for a small onboarding discount and a limited service-credit schedule if thresholds are missed.

Proposal (attached):
- Duration: 30 days from the start of the evaluation window (requested start 2027-09-25)
- Availability tolerance: allow 99.6% availability floor (vs standard 99.9%) for the window
- Service-credit structure (stepped): 5% credit for single-day breaches, 10% for multi-day, 20% cap overall; see attached matrix
- One-time onboarding credit: 15% off first full month of usage if they commit to a paid plan at conclusion

Attachments: SLA-Tolerance-Calc.xlsx, Draft-Addendum-Helix.docx, Service-Credit-Matrix.pdf

Why this is strategic: Helix is a vertical-platform prospect with strong references in healthcare; they want to validate multi-region latency behavior which will drive a larger Dedicated commitment if evaluation goes well. We can limit risk with monitoring hooks, burst caps, and an automatic revert at window close.

Asking for: DealDesk/Exec signoff for the availability variance + tiered credit (legal to finalize) and permission to offer onboarding credit. If you want different caps or a shorter window I can revise — we need a decision by COB 2027-09-21 to hit their test window.

Thanks,
Priya
Director, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

---

+1 on the ask. Quick thoughts:
- 30 days seems ok if we lock in a hard cap on aggregate credits (recommend 20% cap both parties)

- I prefer 45 days only if we get stronger commitment (paid PO or firm go/no-go date)

I've updated the calc to show financial impact at different acceptance levels (see SLA-Tolerance-Calc.xlsx — tab "RiskSizing"). Agree legal should do a quick addendum and finance should confirm the one-time onboarding credit math.

Looping in Jonas for exec signoff on availability variance.

Thanks for the context. Two operational/legal questions before I can sign off:
1) Precedent: have we granted a similar stepped credit structure recently? If so, what was the commercial impact and did it materially affect renewal?
2) Risk controls: confirm instrumentation (traces/alerts) and an automatic cutover to default SLO if abuse detected. We should avoid open-ended variance.

Alternative to consider: a burst throughput allowance for the window (measured in tokens/hour) with no SLA change, plus a capped onboarding credit. That would keep our standard SLA intact while giving the customer headroom. Thoughts?

Provide the answers and a redline of the addendum and I'll provide exec signoff if the cap and guardrails are tight.

Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Request: temporary availability variance + tiered credit for Helix Labs evaluation

Jonas — thanks. Quick answers / updated proposal below.

Precedent: We granted a one-off availability variance last year for a healthcare PoC; outcome: customer converted to Dedicated but the variance window had clear guardrails and a 20% credit cap. Financial impact was <1.1% of that customer's annual run-rate. I pulled the precedent details and attached the excerpts.

Risk controls / instrumentation (what we'll require):
- Real-time p95 and availability dashboards shared with the customer (read-only link)
- Auto-throttle (operational limit) if concurrent sessions exceed agreed threshold
- Automatic revert to standard SLO if anomalies persist for >48 hours without remediation
- Weekly sync for the 30-day window and daily alerting for any threshold breaches

Updated commercial terms (proposal):
- Window: 30 days from 2027-09-25
- Availability floor: 99.6% for the window
- Service-credit schedule (stepped, capped): 5% single-day, 10% multi-day, overall cap 20%
- One-time onboarding credit: 15% off first full month if they convert to paid within 60 days of evaluation close
- If Helix requests sustained higher throughput outside the window we convert to a burst allowance quote and revert SLO to 99.9%

Attachments updated: Draft-Addendum-Helix.docx (redline), SLA-Tolerance-Calc.xlsx (RiskSizing tab updated), Service-Credit-Matrix.pdf

If that's acceptable I'll ask Legal to finalize the addendum and Finance to pre-approve the credit schedule. Need a final yes by 2027-09-21 EOD.

Priya
Director, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
